---
description: Plugin development workflow for AI-DLC Agent Workflow
applyTo: "**"
---

# Plugin Development

- `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/` is the source of truth. Make every agent, skill or manifest change there.
- Never hand-edit `plugins/copilot/**`. After any change under `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/`, run `node tools/build-copilot.mjs`, then confirm `node tools/build-copilot.mjs --check` passes. A Stop hook blocks finishing while it is stale.
- After changing a manifest (`plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`) or adding/removing an agent or skill, run `node tools/validate.mjs`: it syncs the `.claude/` ↔ `.github/` harness twins (`.claude/scripts/sync-harness.mjs`), then runs both validations, and exits 1 when any step fails (`--check` only checks the sync, as CI does):
  - `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code plugin validate --strict ./plugins/claude/ai-dlc`
  - `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code plugin validate --strict .`
- The harness sync is automatic here: one Stop command, `.claude/hooks/stop-sync-then-check.mjs`, runs the harness sync (`sync-harness-on-stop.mjs`) and then the staleness check (`check-copilot-stale.mjs`), in that order, because Claude Code runs the hooks of one event in parallel and the check reads project mirrors (`.claude/skills/<name>/`) the sync can rewrite. The sync reports what it wrote and never blocks; the check blocks while the Copilot plugin is stale. The workflow gate (`check-workflow.mjs`) is a separate Stop hook, independent of both: it reads only `.ai-dlc/`, which the sync never writes. CI runs the sync only with `--check` (`node .claude/scripts/sync-harness.mjs --check`) and fails when anything is pending. Never hand-edit the synced `.github/` twins.
- `.ai-dlc/model-metadata.json` is written only by `.claude/hooks/update-model-metadata.mjs` (its own Stop entry and a `PreToolUse` `Bash` entry for `git commit`; never blocks). The script, its schema and its hook templates come from `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/skills/model-metadata/templates/`: change the template, then copy it to `.claude/hooks/` and `.ai-dlc/` (`tests/model-metadata/` fails while the copies differ).
- After changing a script that has tests in `tests/` (for example `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/skills/workflow/templates/workflow.mjs`) or a test, run `node --test "tests/**/*.test.mjs"` with the glob quoted; CI runs it too. Tests live in `tests/` at the repository root, use only `node:test` and `node:assert`, and are never shipped in the plugin.
- `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/hooks/auto-handoff/` is a Claude-only hooks module (the automatic path of the `handoff` skill's session handoff), adapted from a third-party MIT mod. It imports and registers keep-alive from `hooks/keepalive/`, adapted from another MIT mod; `hooks/hooks.json` lists only auto-handoff. Keep both folders and their `*.test.ts(x)` tests under `hooks/`, never in `skills/`, `agents/` or `scripts/` (the build fails there), and keep `hooks/hooks.json` to `modules`. After changing either, run `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code plugin test ./plugins/claude/ai-dlc` and record the change in that folder's `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Keep agents and generic skills language-agnostic. Stack-specific content (C#, `dotnet`, NuGet, Stryker.NET; TypeScript, `npm`, StrykerJS) belongs in stack-specific skills (`csharp-*`, `nuget-package-deployment`; `ts-*`, `npm-package-deployment`); generic skills route to them through a stack table. Stack-specific rules and hooks are installed into target repositories by skills that `/ai-dlc:init` runs (`dotnet-rules`, `dotnet-test-gate`; `node-rules`, `node-test-gate`), never shipped as plugin-wide hooks.
- Plugin skills that `init` follows are `disable-model-invocation: true`; `init` reads their `SKILL.md` via `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../<skill>/SKILL.md` instead of calling them.
- `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/skills/init/templates/AGENTS.md` is generated by the build from `tools/templates/AGENTS.template.md` plus the body of `agents/orchestrator.md`. Edit those two sources, never the generated file; `--check` fails when it drifts. Likewise `skills/init/templates/CLAUDE.md` and `skills/init/templates/copilot-instructions.md` are rendered from `tools/templates/instructions.template.md` (`<!-- variant:claude|copilot -->` regions).
- `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/skills/plugin-management/templates/build-copilot.mjs` is a generated copy of `tools/build-copilot.mjs`; edit the tool, never the copy. `skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md` documents this repository's setup — update it when the layout, build, CI or dev setup changes.
- Skills that only non-Claude providers need (they stand in for a Claude Code built-in, like `scratchpad`) live in `tools/overlays/non-claude/skills/<name>/`, never under `plugins/claude/ai-dlc/`. The build copies them into the Copilot plugin and fails when one shares a name with a Claude plugin skill.
- A plugin skill that works only in Claude Code (like `cache-keepalive`, which names the hooks module's command, and the `cache-keepalive-install`, `-merge` and `-configure` skills that manage its settings) is listed in `tools/claude-only-skills.json`; the build leaves it out of the Copilot plugin and fails when a listed name is not a plugin skill.
- Skills listed in `tools/project-skills.json` are mirrored by the build into `.claude/skills/<name>/` for repo-local use. The plugin copy is the source; never edit the mirror (`--check` fails when it drifts).
- When a plugin skill mentions an agent, write its default persona name next to its ID on the first prose mention (`**Mark Richards** (`software-architect`)`) and add a `Name` column to tables that list agents. IDs stay the identifiers: never put names in `Agent(...)`, `Skill(...)` args, `subagent_type`, `agent-memory/` paths, frontmatter or fenced code. Default names come from the `Persona name:` line in `agents/*.md`. Skills copied into target repositories as templates keep IDs only, because names can be changed at `/ai-dlc:init`.
- Agent memory (`.claude/agent-memory/`) is committed, here as in every target repository. Never add an ignore rule for it. Before committing a memory file, check that it holds no secrets, credentials, tokens or personal data (`manage-memory`, "Committed with the repository").
